title: QCLI-266's fix is landed on dev and unreleased, so every consumer still runs the broken help
description:
Filed fresh at the orchestrator's ruling rather than by reopening QCLI-266: a Done record is history and stays, and this task is the truth about the shipped package.

QCLI-266 ('help and manifest do not tell a first-time caller how to write a valid task create') was closed Done on 2026-09-11 with all four acceptance criteria checked. The fix is real and it is on dev. No consumer can get it.

Verified 2026-09-11:

  src/application/command-parameters.ts            exists on dev, mtime 2026-09-11 07:50
  grep -c 'command-parameters|valueSyntax' on the installed bundle   -> 0
  npm view @opum-ai/quest versions                 -> ["0.5.0", "0.6.0"]
  npm view @opum-ai/quest dist-tags                -> latest = 0.6.0
  node -p require('./package.json').version        -> 0.6.0

So 0.6.0 is the latest published version AND it predates the fix, while dev's package.json still reads 0.6.0. This is a release gap, not a regression -- but the version string cannot express the difference, which is why it is invisible: `quest --version` reports 0.6.0 for the shipped package and for a dev checkout carrying commits the shipped package does not have. Nothing a caller can run distinguishes them.

How this surfaced, which is the part worth keeping: a session in THIS repository, with the fixed source on disk, hit the exact failure QCLI-266 describes -- three consecutive 'task create received invalid arguments' rejections before working out that --acceptance-criteria takes a single JSON array string and cannot be repeated. It read `quest help task create`, which listed the flag name and said nothing about its value shape, because the binary on PATH is the npm-published 0.6.0. The repository is not a witness to its own fixes.

That is the same class as QCLI-269's second half and as the reported OMARK-42 traps: a surface that a caller reasonably trusts reporting something that is not true of the thing they are actually running.

Scope is a patch release off dev. The provenance gate from QCLI-267 (scripts/qualification/release-provenance.mjs, --pre before publishing) is already wired into the release workflow and must pass rather than be worked around; docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md carries the procedure. Publishing to a registry is in the fleet's irreversible set, so the publish step needs the user's direct authority, not an orchestrator's -- that approval is part of this task, not an obstacle to filing it.

Worth settling while here, since it is what made the gap silent: whether a dev checkout should report a version distinguishable from the last published one. Not a blocker for the release, and should not grow into one.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND CONFIRMED, 2026-09-13, with kernel-log evidence plus a controlled reversible experiment.

Captured `log stream` (predicate on process==git / SIGKILL / sandbox / syspolicy / amfid / Xprotect) while reproducing the kill with `git hash-object npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest`. The kernel logged, at the exact moment of the kill:

  kernel: CODE SIGNING: cs_invalid_page(0x10d820000): p=15781[git] final status 0x23000200, denying page sending SIGKILL
  kernel: CODE SIGNING: process 15781[git]: rejecting invalid page at address 0x10d820000 from offset 0x3d24000 in file ".../npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest" (cs_mtime:... == mtime:...) (signed:1 validated:0 tainted:1 nx:1 wpmapped:0 dirty:0 depth:0)

This is macOS's AMFI/code-signing page-validation subsystem, not an EDR, not the sandbox tool, not a volume property, not OOM. Mechanism: this file is a signed (adhoc, linker-signed) Mach-O executable. When git mmaps it (which it does internally to hash/diff/add large files), the kernel validates each mapped page against the embedded CodeDirectory. If the file's on-disk bytes were changed by overwriting an EXISTING inode in place (truncate+rewrite, e.g. a build tool re-linking to the same output path across repeated local builds) rather than by unlinking and creating a fresh file, the kernel can be left with stale per-vnode code-signing validation state for that inode. A later mmap sees pages that fail validation against that stale state ("tainted"), and the kernel denies the mapping and SIGKILLs the accessing process as an anti-tampering defense -- working as designed, just against a build workflow that happens to trip it.

This explains every earlier observation at once:
- New file (scratch repo, ditto copy) never fails: a new path/inode has no prior code-signing cache to go stale.
- The real worktree fails on BOTH volumes: it's an inode property, not a volume property (the earlier "it is the volume" test actually varied inode-freshness via cp-vs-ditto/scratch-vs-real-repo, not volume, as already corrected).
- Only the darwin-arm64 binary is affected, never the other 5 platform binaries of comparable size in the same tree: only darwin-arm64 is a Mach-O signed for THIS host's architecture: the kernel's Mach-O code-signing page validation has no reason to engage with an ELF (linux) or PE (win32) file, or a Mach-O for a different architecture.
- `git cat-file -p HEAD:<path>` (reads the compressed blob from .git/objects, never mmaps a Mach-O with an embedded signature) is unaffected -- confirmed again this session, exit 0.

CONFIRMED WITH A REVERSIBLE EXPERIMENT, content integrity verified throughout (sha256 4e56fc67e5880fd630e000197cf928ceabaa80c66fc4891175243c39fbc16bcc unchanged before/after):
1. Backed up the current working-tree file (the qualified 0.6.1 darwin-arm64 build, confirmed by hash) to the scratchpad.
2. `rm` the tracked working-tree file (inode 37329524) and recreated it at the same path from the backup bytes (new inode 37337600) -- unlink-then-create, not truncate-in-place.
3. `git hash-object npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest` -- previously reliably SIGKILLed -- now exits 0, producing blob f975ddadc613aaf1a2273ec6c21153fbaf4aa431. This is the exact same blob hash the orchestrator's own earlier "boot-volume scratch dir" test produced -- because that test's `cp` there also happened to create a fresh inode, which was the real variable all along, not the volume.

Working tree right now: npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest holds the correct, byte-verified 0.6.1 build, on a fresh inode, executable bit set, and ordinary git operations on it now work. Nothing has been staged, added, committed, or pushed. Standing by per the standing instruction -- reporting this to the orchestrator/user before resuming the release plan (git add / commit / PR), since "nobody ships or bypasses until we know what the SIGKILL actually is" was explicit and I want that lifted in words, not assumed, even though the finding is now solid.

FIX FOR THE FUTURE (belongs in QCLI-275 and/or docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md regardless of which packaging shape wins): never overwrite a signed macOS Mach-O binary in place at a fixed path across repeated local builds. Always unlink first, or build to a temp path and atomically rename into place, so a fresh inode is allocated and no stale kernel code-signing validation state can apply. This is a general macOS build-tooling gotcha, not specific to Bun or to git.
